## Repository structure

This is a multi-plugin marketplace repository. The root `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` lists all plugins, and each plugin has its own manifest:

```
plugins/
├── .cursor-plugin/
│   └── marketplace.json       # Marketplace manifest (lists all plugins)
├── plugin-name/
│   ├── .cursor-plugin/
│   │   └── plugin.json        # Per-plugin manifest
│   ├── skills/                # Agent skills (SKILL.md with frontmatter)
│   ├── rules/                 # Cursor rules (.mdc files)
│   ├── mcp.json               # MCP server definitions
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── CHANGELOG.md
│   └── LICENSE
└── ...
```

# Advisor

You are the main model. Advisor mode adds a second, stronger model that you consult at a few key points. The advisor gets your briefing (and the full transcript when available), thinks hard, and returns a verdict with guidance. It does not edit files. You still do the work and make the final call.

State lives in `.cursor/advisor/state.json` at the project root. When that file exists with `"enabled": true`, advisor mode is on for this project.

# text-to-cad

The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models
as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks,
generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal
and CNC fabrication services.

It is supported by all popular agents that support plugins or the
[skills](https://skills.sh) framework, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
Gemini and Grok.

## 💻 Install

### Ask your agent (recommended)

Send this message to your agent and it will install text-to-cad for you.

```text
Install text-to-cad from https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad
```

By default, text-to-cad sends usage stats and crash reports, tagged with a random
ID and never including your files, paths or prompts; turn them off with
`uvx cadgen telemetry off`, or ask your agent to. [Telemetry](#telemetry) says
the rest.

Or install it yourself:

1. CAD runs through [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): check that it is installed
   (`uv --version`), and if it is missing, install it with
   [uv's installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
2. Run the commands under your agent app's heading below, or under
   [Other Agents](#other-agents) if it has none.
3. Restart the app. Its first start downloads CAD's runtime, so it needs a network
   connection.

The plugin for your agent app brings the skills and CAD's viewer, a local server
(`cadgen mcp`). For an agent without a plugin, install the skills alone. Install
one or the other in an app, not both: two copies means every skill twice.

The install commands below take the `latest` branch: it holds the plugin alone
and gets each release once it is on PyPI. `main`, where development happens,
installs too, but can hold changes that aren't released yet. Each app names the
branch in its own way (`#latest`, `--ref latest`, `@latest` or
`--branch latest`); leave it out and the app installs `main`.

Each app's heading also says how to update text-to-cad, and how to reinstall it:
remove it, then install it again. Updating the plugin updates CAD: the new
release's cadgen is downloaded the first time it runs, and the skills and the
server share it. Earlier releases stay in uv's cache until you run `uv cache prune`.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad#latest
claude plugin install text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

The plugin also starts CAD's server. Where Claude Code can show app views, CAD
shows models as viewer cards in the conversation; otherwise, as in a terminal,
asking it to show a model gives you a link that opens the model in the CAD
Viewer in your browser.

To update, run these, then restart Claude Code:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update earthtojake
claude plugin update text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again:

```bash
claude plugin uninstall text-to-cad@earthtojake
claude plugin marketplace remove earthtojake
```

### Claude Desktop

CAD shows models in the chat: ask Claude to show one and it appears as a viewer
card you can orbit, add to your prompt, and open full size; Claude can read what
you selected and see what you see. It runs locally through uv: add the server to
Claude Desktop's config (Settings > Developer > Edit Config), then restart the
app. If Claude Desktop cannot find `uvx`, give its full path (`which uvx`).

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cad": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--no-config", "--managed-python", "--python", "3.13", "--from", "cadgen==0.7.20", "cadgen", "mcp"],
      "env": {"CADGEN_INSTALL_CHANNEL": "claude-desktop"}
    }
  }
}
```

The config pins a cadgen release in `args`, and uvx keeps the version it first
downloads. To update, change that version to the
[latest release](https://pypi.org/project/cadgen/), then restart Claude Desktop.

### Codex

Install text-to-cad from Codex's plugin directory:
[text-to-cad for Codex](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6ac09476ef008191a35887b22b0d048a),
then **Open in desktop app**.

In the Codex app the plugin also brings the CAD viewer: **CAD** in the sidebar
(recent models, and Open), a **CAD** tab beside each thread that the agent
drives, and *Open with CAD* for model files.

<details>
<summary>Manual install</summary>

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad --ref latest
codex plugin add text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

To update, upgrade the `earthtojake` marketplace (or use Plugins › Manage ›
Marketplace), then restart Codex:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace upgrade earthtojake
```

To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again:

=== cadgen pyproject ===
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "cadgen"
version = "0.7.20"
description = "STEP-first CAD artifact generation runtime: build123d STEP/GLB/topology generation, validation, and inspection for CAD agent skills."
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [{ name = "earthtojake" }]
keywords = ["cad", "step", "glb", "build123d", "parametric", "agent-skills"]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Intended Audience :: Manufacturing",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Topic :: Multimedia :: Graphics :: 3D Modeling",
  "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
]
# ezdxf and shapely both look transitive through build123d, and both are kept
# DIRECT on purpose: cadgen imports each one itself, so each is its own
# dependency regardless of who else happens to pull it in.
#
# ezdxf stopped being a WRITING dependency when @dxf moved to build123d geometry
# (cadgen._internal.dxf_emit) -- the engine writes through build123d's ExportDXF
# and no author-facing contract mentions ezdxf. It remains a READING one, which
# is not going away: cadgen.drawing_payload flattens a .dxf to draw it (for the
# Viewer's pane and for `cadgen dxf snapshot` alike), and cadgen.drawing_checks
# parses one to validate it post-hoc. A DXF reader needs a DXF parser. Dropping the declaration would leave those two modules resting on
# build123d's own dependency list, and they would fail at a user's runtime, not
# at install, the day that list changes.
#
# shapely is likewise narrower than it was -- flatten's unions and offsets are
# OCC operations now, with shapely only the fallback for the degenerate unions
# OCC refuses -- but a fallback that is not installed is not a fallback.
dependencies = [
  # Bounded above on purpose. cadgen does not merely CALL build123d, it
  # reaches into it: the determinism shim shadows `set` in three topology
  # modules and replaces `Vertex.__hash__`, and the lazy store replaces
  # `Compound.__init__` and reads its arguments BY POSITION. A minor release
  # is free to reorder that signature or rename those choke points, and the
  # failure mode is silent: a patch that no longer matches simply stops
  # applying. Raise the ceiling deliberately, after re-running the suite
  # against the new minor.
  "build123d>=0.11.1,<0.12",
  # cadgen imports OCP directly for STEP/XCAF, topology and BREP work.  Match
  # build123d's non-VTK provider: cadgen does not import VTK or cadquery, and
  # this keeps the optional visualization stack out of every CAD install.
  "cadquery-ocp-novtk>=7.9,<8",
  "ezdxf",
  # @eng_drawing renders its PDF through ezdxf's drawing add-on, whose
  # matplotlib backend is the page renderer. The add-on also imports Pillow at
  # module level and ezdxf declares neither, so a cadgen module would otherwise
  # import packages cadgen does not depend on -- and the drawing IS the PDF, so
  # neither is optional.

message) and how long they took, which features were used -- added up over a few minutes before they are sent, each
batch under a random ID of its own and the time it was made, so one sent again is counted once. When cadgen's own
code fails, they also send a crash report: the error's type and where in cadgen (or Python, or one of its

one process, and `CADGEN_TELEMETRY=1` on, without changing your setting; nothing is sent by default in CI or from a
development install. Nothing waits to send: what a command counts without the build daemon, and what any part of
cadgen counted since its last send when it exits, waits in small files in cadgen's state folder until the next part

### Windows 11: Smart App Control

The CAD kernel behind the `cad`, `dxf`, `urdf`, `srdf` and `sdf`
skills is `OCP`, OpenCascade's Python binding, and its wheel ships an unsigned
native module. Windows 11's Smart App Control blocks unsigned native code, so
on a machine where it is on (the default on a fresh install) every `cadgen`
command and `import build123d` fails with
`ImportError: DLL load failed while importing OCP`, and Event Viewer records
the refusal as Event ID 3077 under CodeIntegrity › Operational. `cadgen doctor`
names this when it sees it.

Smart App Control has no per-app exception. Either turn it off (Settings ›
Privacy & security › Windows Security › App & browser control › Smart App
Control settings; once off it can only be turned back on by reinstalling
Windows) or run the CAD skills under WSL, where it does not apply. The wheel
is built by the cadquery-ocp project, so signing it is not something this
repository can do.

## 🧰 Skills

Install the library to give agents focused workflows for CAD, fabrication,
robot description files, simulation, and local review.

| Skill        | Summary                                                                                                                                            | Source                                              |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| CAD          | Creates and edits CAD models from plain-language or image requests, with STEP as the main output along with options to export to STL, 3MF and GLB. | [skills/cad](skills/cad/SKILL.md)                   |
| step.parts   | Finds off-the-shelf STEP parts like screws, bearings, motors, and connectors.                                                                      | [skills/step-parts](skills/step-parts/SKILL.md)     |
| Engineering Drawing | Dimensioned engineering drawings from a part, as a PDF: views, hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts, title block. | [skills/engineering-drawing](skills/engineering-drawing/SKILL.md) |
| DXF          | Creates 2D DXF drawings like profiles, templates, gaskets, and cut layouts from Python sources or CAD geometry.                                    | [skills/dxf](skills/dxf/SKILL.md)                   |
| URDF         | Writes robot structure files with links, joints, limits, inertials, and meshes.                                                                    | [skills/urdf](skills/urdf/SKILL.md)                 |
| SRDF         | Adds MoveIt planning groups, end effectors, poses, and collision rules to a URDF.                                                                  | [skills/srdf](skills/srdf/SKILL.md)                 |
| SDF          | Creates simulator models and worlds with frames, physics, sensors, and lights.                                                                     | [skills/sdf](skills/sdf/SKILL.md)                   |
| SendCutSend  | Checks DXF and STEP files before upload to SendCutSend.                                                                                            | [skills/sendcutsend](skills/sendcutsend/SKILL.md)   |
| DfAM Check   | Measures mesh printability per process: wall thickness, overhangs, support volume, and build orientation.                                          | [skills/dfam-check](skills/dfam-check/SKILL.md)     |
| DFM | Reviews a part for sheet metal, CNC machining, or injection molding, with measured evidence and the cited rule behind every finding; measures draft, undercuts and projected area from a mesh. | [skills/dfm](skills/dfm/SKILL.md) |
| G-code       | Slices models into printer-ready G-code with OrcaSlicer, using your own printer presets.                                                           | [skills/gcode](skills/gcode/SKILL.md)               |
| Bambu Labs   | Sends prints to Bambu Lab printers through Bambu Connect, Bambu Lab's official app, or Bambu Studio.                                               | [skills/bambu-labs](skills/bambu-labs/SKILL.md)     |

The store contains only derived results\n\n`~/.cache/cadgen` is the store: content-addressed objects (a model's result\ntree and the components it is made of) and input-addressed index entries\n(the per-model record, the document → tree map, bounds and tessellation\nentries) — data derivable from sources and documents, and nothing else. Its\nlayout, formats, gate, two-sides law and invariants are the contract in\n[`STORE.md`](STORE.md); read it before touching anything that writes to or\nreads from the store. Where this document and `STORE.md` disagree, `STORE.md`\nis right and this one is stale.\n\n*Pressure-test*: everything in the store is (a) a pure function of some\nsource or document, (b) safely deletable at any time, and (c) rebuildable\nby running the models again. If losing a store entry would lose information,\nthat information is in the wrong place.\n\n**The store is what the sources imply; the sidecar is what the author meant.**\n\nThe store holds itself to a size cap (`CADGEN_STORE_MAX`, default 20 GB): the\ndaemon, when idle, evicts derived entries (mesh, surface, component, bounds,\ndrawing) least recently written first and sweeps what nothing reaches, and\nretires on sight the index kinds an older cadgen left (`index/op`). A record,\na document entry or an output entry is never evicted. `cadgen store gc` does\nthe same by hand (`STORE.md` §8). A cadgen never judges what it cannot read:\na store a newer cadgen wrote to within 30 days is left to that cadgen, and a\nfolder it does not know is never touched. A read never writes the store, and a write\nthat finds its bytes already present claims them, so deletion needs no\ncoordination: a sweep keeps whatever a publish has claimed, and a racing\nreader re-misses and rebuilds. Store correctness needs\nno lock protocol: atomic writes, pins and the publish rule (`STORE.md` §5, §7)\ndecide concurrent outcomes. Saved-file readers never wait for a source model\nto finish; missing derived artifacts are resolved through the build pool.\n*Pressure-test*: build a model and snapshot it, make the store read-only, then\ndo both again: each succeeds and nothing under the store changes.\n\n### 3. One sidecar per artifact, and it belongs to that artifact alone\n\n`part.step` gets `part.step.json` — schema-versioned sections (kinematics,\nappearance, animation). New capability = new section + schema bump, never a second sidecar\nfile. Model-side, beside the artifact, so it travels with the file it\ndescribes — and it exists only when law 17 says it must.\n\nA sidecar describes the model that declared it — never its parent, never its\nchildren. A parent composing a child receives geometry and intrinsic appearance\n(tree, labels, colors, PBR values, placements, exact shape). The child's\nkinematics belong to the child's own sidecar,\nand an assembly that needs a relation declares it on the assembly. This is\nwhat lets a cached child stand in for its function: the cache carries\ngeometry and intrinsic appearance; a parent never reads the child's sidecar.\n*Pressure-test*: build a child that declares `kinematics=`, then build a parent\nthat composes it. Zero metadata in written artifacts\n\nA STEP or DXF is pure geometry. Provenance, kinematics, and context ride\nthe sidecar; the artifact separated from everything else is a plain\nimportable file.\n\n### 5. Byte determinism is the writers' promise, not the kernel's\n\ncadgen's writers are pure: the same shapes give the same bytes, in every\nformat — STEP (canonicalized NAUO ids and presentation-style ordering), meshes\n(one deterministic tessellator), DXF (geometry-ordered emitter). The geometry\nkernel makes no such promise. Two runs of one model can differ in a last digit\nor in the order of the pieces a boolean returns, and cadgen neither hides that\nnor depends on it. Equal bytes mean reuse; different bytes cost a\nrecomputation (a re-mesh, a parent recompose) and never a wrong answer. A\nrebuild whose writer input is unchanged keeps its saved STEP instead of writing\nthe same bytes again ([`STORE.md`](STORE.md) §3, `writerInput`).\nContent addresses stay byte hashes; whether a model runs is decided by its\nsources (`STORE.md` §4), never by its outputs being reproducible. Compare two\nbuilds by geometry within a tolerance, never by file hash.\n*Pressure-test*: build one model twice, each from an empty store. If the bytes\ndiffer, nothing fails, and the second build's outputs are as correct as the\nfirst's.\n\n### 6. One surface, three faces\n\nThe DECORATOR declares a capability on a model, the PUBLIC FUNCTION\n(`cadgen.<format>.<verb>`) performs it, and the CLI (`cadgen <format>\n<verb>`) is GENERATED from the function's signature\n(`_internal/cli_from_function.py`) — never hand-written, structurally\nsync-tested.\n\n*Pressure-test*: for any option, \
build123d geometry; `read_scene(path)` returns\nrevision-scoped occurrence/selector views with caller-owned world geometry.\n`cadgen.geometry` provides `closest_points`, `overlap_volume`, `is_sound`,\n`topology_errors`, `boundary_edges`, `self_intersections` and\n`mass_properties`. These operations accept native geometry and return facts;\nselection, units, thresholds, exclusions and verdicts belong to the caller's\nscript. The import path\ninside a build is exactly `python script.py`'s — the script's own folder, then\nthe caller's `PYTHONPATH` — and nothing cadgen adds or infers from directory\nnames. No backwards compatibility\n\nHard cutovers only. Every retired surface fails loudly with a teaching\nerror naming its replacement — never an alias, never a shim.\n\nThe explicit exception is `cadgen.assembly.AssemblyHelper`: it is softly\ndeprecated and still works. Construction emits a visible `FutureWarning`\npointing to native build123d compounds, labels, transforms and joints.\nImporting it is quiet; a current model that skips its body emits no warning.\nThis does not change geometry, model freshness or child sharing.\n\n### 9. Closed vocabularies\n\nEvery declaration surface has a closed key/kind set. Unknown keys are\nteaching errors, never silently ignored.\n\n### 10. Loud failure or correct output, nothing between\n\nThe cardinal sin is plausible-wrong output at exit 0. No silent fallbacks,\nno globs, no guessing; a failed render leaves NO file at the requested\npath.\n\n### 11–14. A build's status\n(STORE §9b) carries no geometry: clients render the saved file.\nCorrectness never depends on a\nstore hit (13). Composition: importing binds, calling links — a parent\ndepends on a child by its RESULT (the pinned tree) and on what importing it\nruns in the parent's process (its module body and model headers, never a\nmodel body), on a constant by its VALUE, on a helper by its REACH (the part of\nthe helper the script and every file the build executed can run, closed\nstatically; the whole file — or the whole closure — wherever the analysis\ncannot see), on a data file by its BYTES (every file the build opened,\nwhoever opened it: STORE.md §5, every read is seen),\nand on every file whose appearance would change what an import finds\n([`STORE.md`](STORE.md) §3) — and a model must never `read_step` its own\noutput (14). The bundled runtime\nunder `_runtime/` is the JS half of these; the laws' JS statements live in that\nruntime. It is built\nwhen the wheel is packaged and travels only inside it: the source tree never\ncarries a built copy, so an installed cadgen and the sources that produced it\ncannot disagree.\n\n### 15. The package ships alone\n\nThe installed distribution is the whole world: the Python engine, the\nbundled `_runtime/`, and this document. It works with the repository it\nwas built from gone — and its markdown must read that way, referring to\nnothing outside the package.\n\n*Pressure-test*: every sentence in the package's markdown must be true and\nactionable for someone who only ran `pip install cadgen`. Naming a bundled\nthing (\
build123d's `==` and `is_same` answer. A script therefore behaves the\nsame inside cadgen as under plain Python. The hooks that remain change no\nresult: `determinism.py` fixes the iteration order of build123d's\nde-duplications (an order-keeping set, and a `Vertex` hash by point that\nleaves equality alone), lazy children defer a child's geometry until it is\nread (`STORE.md` §9a), and the file trace only watches what the run opens\n(`STORE.md` §5). An expensive or independently edited part gets its\nspeed by being its own model, never from a cache inside one. What an older\ncadgen cached inside a run (`index/op`, the operation cache) is never read,\nand is retired with every object only it named (`STORE.md` §8).\n*Pressure-test*: call a model's function under plain Python and inside a\ncadgen build; the geometry it returns, and the answer to every `==` and\n`is_same` along the way, are the same.\n\n### 19. Nothing waits on the network\n\nOnce installed, cadgen works offline: every command, build, snapshot, server\nand page. Its own requests are two: telemetry\n(`analytics.py`, usage counts under a random id, sent by default once a `cadgen`\ncommand has said so, and never after the person's no) and the daily version check\n(`updates.py`). Both run in the background and fail silently: no start,\ncommand, build, request or tool call waits on them, and one that fails changes\nnothing but what is counted or offered. A command sends nothing itself: it hands\nwhat it counted -- a build it made with no daemon to ask, a snapshot, a drawing, a\ncrash -- to a running build daemon over its local socket, never starting one, and\ngives up after a moment (`daemon.client.HAND_OVER_SECONDS`); with no daemon to take\nit, it keeps it in a small file beside the settings for the next process that sends\n(`analytics.spool`). A process that exits sends nothing either: its last batch --\na server's, or the build daemon's -- is kept in a file beside the settings, and the\nnext process that sends sends it in the background, a moment after it starts\n(`analytics.KEPT`). One wait remains, bounded, for something only the network can\ndo: `cadgen telemetry off`, which waits for the deletion it asks for (still owed,\nand asked again, when nobody answers). The\npages load nothing from the internet: everything they show ships in the wheel.\nInstalling needs the network (cadgen itself, and the headless browser the first\nsnapshot fetches), and nothing after it does. The law is the package's, not the\nlauncher's: a launcher that checks a package index before it starts anything\n(`uvx`, once its cache is stale) has its own needs.\n*Pressure-test*: with an installed cadgen and every request refused (a proxy on\na closed port), and again with every request hanging, start a server, open a\nview, call each tool, and run a build and a snapshot: each works, and nothing\nwaits on a request beyond the two waits above.\n\n## The shape of the package\n\n```\nsrc/cadgen/\n  <format>.py            # public namespaces: step, stl, threemf, glb, dxf,\n                         #   urdf, srdf, sdf — each binds its verbs\n  authoring.py           # @step/@dxf/@stl/@glb/@threemf decorators; a call\n                         #   builds at top level and composes (a lazy child)\n                         #   inside a body; a model's outputs are what they\n                         #   declare — a mesh decorator alone is a model that\n                         #   writes no STEP\n  kinematics.py          # typed mates vocabulary (revolute/slider/\n                         #   cylindrical/fastened, couple, normalize)\n  step_scene.py          # read_step and read_scene\n  assembly.py            # label utilities and softly deprecated AssemblyHelper\n  results.py             # the typed Results every verb returns (stdlib-only)\n  settings.py            # the person's settings: settings.json in the state\n                         #   directory, a section per feature, shared by\n                         #   every app and version of cadgen\n  analytics.py           # telemetry: usage counts and crash reports (a\n                         #   crash's type and frames, never its message) from\n                         #   the CAD apps and the build daemon, on by default\n                         #   once a command has said so, never after a no (its\n                         #   answer: settings.json's `telemetry` section)\n  features.py            # the CAD views' features a person can turn off\n                         #   (Quick edit: settings.json's `features` section)\n  updates.py             # the daily version check: whether a newer release is\n                         #   out, for a copy nothing else keeps up to date\n                         #   (_internal/channel.py)\n  store/                 # the store (STORE.md): objects, index, records, trees,\n                         #   closure, gate, materialize, publish, lazy, gc, view\n  cli/                   # generated command shells, one per <format> <verb>\n  cli_tree.py            # the build tree on stderr / JSONL events\n  daemon/                # the build pool: executors (daemon + transient),\n                         #   broker (job slots, coalescing), pool (workers,\n                         #   spares, extras), jobs (the ledger), server,\n                         #   worker, client, transport, telemetry (what it\n                         #   builds and how that goes, counted)\n  _internal/             # the engine: generation pipeline, tree builder,\n                         #   filetrace (every file a build opens),\n                         #   FK (kinematics_fk/resolve), mesh_export ledger,\n                         #   cli_from_function, doors (documents by bytes),\n                         #   source_sidecar, step_assemble/step_reemit\n  viewer/                # the CAD Viewer's server: launcher (main),\n                         #   routes (http_app), files by absolute path\n                         #   (backend), a file's catalog row (scanner; started\n                         #   when a watched build saves: warm), the explorer's\n                         #   reads (folders), the model library every CAD view\n                         #   shares (recents), status\n                         #   (artifact_status: not compiled / compiling /\n                         #   compiled / failed), build_progress (the daemon's\n                         #   job ledger, read over its socket)\n  mcp/                   # CAD for agent hosts: stdio JSON-RPC (protocol), the\n                         #   tools and launches (server), open views (views),\n                         #   the viewer routes in-process (tunnel), roots,\n                         #   the page (ui), and the CAD Viewer link for\n                         #   a host that renders no MCP Apps (browser)\n  _runtime/              # BUILT JS (browser snapshot renderer, node\n                         #   builders, the viewer client, the MCP app page)\n                         #   and the native file tracer, one library per\n                         #   platform — produced when the wheel is packaged,\n                         #   never committed, never edited\n```\n\nVerbs by format: `step` compile · build · snapshot;\n`stl`/`3mf`/`glb` build · snapshot; `dxf` snapshot; `urdf`/`sdf`\nvalidate · snapshot; `srdf` validate. `cadgen snapshot` routes any suffix.\n`cadgen store|daemon|doctor` are status commands, `cadgen viewer\n[stop]` the CAD Viewer's launcher, and `cadgen mcp`\nthe server an agent host starts — all deliberately outside the mirror pattern. `cadgen step compile` is internal tooling: skills never\nteach it — doors compile a document's missing tree on demand.\n\nDeveloped in [earthtojake/text-to-cad](https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad);\nthat repo's contributor guide carries the development workflow (tests,\nbundling, versioning).\n\nThe viewer exposes `POST /__cad/clipboard` for explicit viewport PNG copies. It\nuses the same host and custom-header POST gates as other mutation routes, limits\nimages to 20 MiB, and delegates native delivery to `viewer/clipboard.py`. It never\nreads the clipboard. Unsupported desktop clipboard environments return an error.\n\nIt exposes `POST /__cad/sketches?name=` for a picture a copied prompt names by path:\nthe view with a person's sketch drawn over it. ## 一、cursor/plugins

1. **市场清单**：`.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`（19 KB），含 **100 个插件条目**；另有 `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` 仅 1 条（origin-apps）。条目字段：`name`、`source`（插件目录相对路径）、`description`，个别带 `minClientVersions`（如 finance：`{"cursor":"never","grokbot":"0.49.0"}`）。Schema：`schemas/marketplace.schema.json`（required: name+source）。
2. **是标准 SKILL.md**。例 1 `advisor/skills/advisor/SKILL.md`：
```
---
name: advisor
description: >-
  Advisor mode. Consult a stronger (or different) model at key checkpoints:
  before major decisions, when stuck on an error, and before declaring a task
  done. Use when the user types /advisor, ...
icon: lightbulb
color: purple
---
```
例 2 `cli-for-agent/skills/cli-for-agents/SKILL.md`：`name: cli-for-agents` + 折叠 description。即标准 name/description + 正文，但可出现非标准键（icon/color/license）。
3. **安装机制**：README 全文**无任何安装命令、无外链**，只有插件表、目录结构、"## License MIT"；安装由宿主客户端驱动（schema 说明 `minClientVersions` = 客户端安装所需最低版本，可设 `never` 对某客户端完全隐藏）。仓库内只有校验器 `scripts/validate-plugins.mjs` + `.github/workflows/validate-plugins.yml`。技能正文是通用 agent-skills 格式，但大量插件含 Cursor 专用件：`agents/`、`hooks/hooks.json`、`.cursor-plugin/plugin.json`、`rules/*.mdc`、`mcp.json`；advisor 的 SKILL.md 直接读写项目根 `.cursor/advisor/state.json` → **技能正文可移植，hooks/agents/宿主目录不可**。
4. **许可**：根目录**无 LICENSE 文件**；各插件自带 LICENSE（advisor、cli-for-agent、third_party/gmail 均为 MIT, © 2026 Cursor）；README 末尾仅一行 "## License MIT"。
5. **分类/目录名**：分类（README Category 列）= Developer Tools / Utilities / Productivity / Integrations。目录：根级 17 个（advisor、agent-compatibility、cli-for-agent、continual-learning、create-plugin、cursor-sdk、cursor-team-kit、docs-canvas、dyl-stack、grok-voice、orchestrate、origin-apps、pr-review-canvas、pstack、ralph-loop、teaching、thermos）+ `third_party/`（约 95 个，如 gmail、github、playwright、salesforce、zoom）。

## 二、earthtojake/text-to-cad

1. **三种入口并存**：MCP server（`mcp.json`、`codex.mcp.json`：`uvx --no-config --managed-python --python 3.13 --from cadgen==0.7.20 cadgen mcp`，stdio JSON-RPC）；`skills/` 下 12 个技能；CLI `cadgen <format> <verb>`（step/stl/3mf/glb/dxf/urdf/srdf/sdf，另有 doctor/viewer/store）。
2. **依赖与体积**（`packages/cadgen/pyproject.toml`）：build123d>=0.11.1,<0.12、cadquery-ocp-novtk>=7.9,<8（几何内核 OCP）、ezdxf、shapely、playwright、matplotlib/Pillow；`skills/dfam-check/requirements.txt` 另需 trimesh、numpy、rtree、scipy、networkx、lxml；`requirements-dev.txt` 需 uv、ziglang。体积：PyPI 上 OCP wheel ≈ 87.1 MB（83 MiB），cadgen wheel ≈ 11.6 MB（字段 `size`），外加首次快照下载的无头浏览器；**README 未给总量数字**，只说"首启会下载 CAD runtime，需要联网"。
3. **许可**：仓库 MIT（Copyright (c) 2026 Thompson Labs LLC，`LICENSE`）；SKILL.md 内 `license: MIT`。README **未写** OCCT/OCP 授权（只提 OCP wheel 未签名、Win11 Smart App Control 会拦截并报 `DLL load failed while importing OCP`）；PyPI 元数据 `cadquery-ocp-novtk` 与 `build123d` 均标 **Apache-2.0**；OCCT 本体授权**需另行核查**。
4. **产出格式**：STEP（主）、STL、3MF、GLB，另有 DXF 与工程图 PDF。
5. **制造性检查**：`skills/dfm` 做钣金/CNC/注塑审查（实测证据 + 引用规则，从 mesh 量 draft/undercut/projected area），并自述 "a guided review skill, not an automatic feature-recognition or manufacturing certification engine"；`skills/dfam-check` 量 mesh 可打印性（壁厚、悬垂、支撑体积、摆放方向）。

来源：`cursor/plugins` 的 README.md、.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json、.claude-plugin/marketplace.json、schemas/marketplace.schema.json、advisor/{.cursor-plugin/plugin.json,skills/advisor/SKILL.md,LICENSE}、cli-for-agent/skills/cli-for-agents/SKILL.md；`earthtojake/text-to-cad` 的 README.md、LICENSE、mcp.json、codex.mcp.json、.codex-plugin/plugin.json、skills.sh.json、packages/cadgen/pyproject.toml、skills/{cad,dfm,dfam-check}/*（均 `raw.githubusercontent.com/.../main/` 路径）；体积数据来自 `pypi.org/pypi/{cadquery-ocp-novtk,cadgen}/json`。

# Cursor plugins

Official Cursor plugins for popular developer tools, frameworks, and SaaS products. Each plugin is a standalone directory at the repository root with its own `.cursor-plugin/plugin.json` manifest.

## Plugins

| `name` | Plugin | Author | Category | `description` (from marketplace) |
|:-------|:-------|:-------|:---------|:-------------------------------------|
| `teaching` | [Teaching](teaching/) | Cursor | Utilities | Skill mapping, practice plans, and learning retrospectives. |
| `continual-learning` | [Continual Learning](continual-learning/) | Eric Zakariasson | Developer Tools | Incremental transcript-driven memory updates for AGENTS.md using high-signal bullet points only. |
| `cursor-team-kit` | [Cursor Team Kit](cursor-team-kit/) | Eric Zakariasson | Developer Tools | Internal team workflows for CI, code review, shipping, local automation, and verification. |
| `thermos` | [Thermos](thermos/) | Cursor | Developer Tools | Thermo-nuclear branch review: deep security/correctness audits, harsh code-quality rubrics, parallel subagents, thermos orchestration, and optional merge-ready PR flows. |
| `create-plugin` | [Create Plugin](create-plugin/) | Cursor | Developer Tools | Scaffold and validate new agent plugins. |
| `ralph-loop` | [Ralph Loop](ralph-loop/) | Cursor | Developer Tools | Iterative self-referential AI loops using the Ralph Wiggum technique. |
| `agent-compatibility` | [Agent Compatibility](agent-compatibility/) | Cursor | Developer Tools | CLI-backed repo compatibility scans plus agents that audit startup, validation, and docs against reality. |
| `cli-for-agent` | [CLI for Agents](cli-for-agent/) | Eric Zakariasson | Developer Tools | Patterns for designing CLIs that coding agents can run reliably: flags, help with examples, pipelines, errors, idempotency, dry-run. |
| `pr-review-canvas` | [PR Review Canvas](pr-review-canvas/) | Cursor | Developer Tools | Render PR diffs as review canvases grouped by importance. |

## Repository structure

This is a multi-plugin marketplace repository. The root `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` lists all plugins, and each plugin has its own manifest:

```
plugins/
├── .cursor-plugin/
│   └── marketplace.json       # Marketplace manifest (lists all plugins)
├── plugin-name/
│   ├── .cursor-plugin/
│   │   └── plugin.json        # Per-plugin manifest
│   ├── skills/                # Agent skills (SKILL.md with frontmatter)
│   ├── rules/                 # Cursor rules (.mdc files)
│   ├── mcp.json               # MCP server definitions
│   ├── README.md
│   ├── CHANGELOG.md
│   └── LICENSE
└── ...
```

---
name: advisor
description: >-
  Advisor mode. Consult a stronger (or different) model at key checkpoints:
  before major decisions, when stuck on an error, and before declaring a task
  done. Use when the user types /advisor, asks to turn the advisor on or off,
  picks an advisor model, or explicitly asks for a second opinion from a
  stronger or different model. Never enable it on your own.
icon: lightbulb
color: purple
---

# Advisor

You are the main model. Advisor mode adds a second, stronger model that you consult at a few key points. The advisor gets your briefing (and the full transcript when available), thinks hard, and returns a verdict with guidance. It does not edit files. You still do the work and make the final call.

State lives in `.cursor/advisor/state.json` at the project root. When that file exists with `"enabled": true`, advisor mode is on for this project.

# text-to-cad

The text-to-cad plugin gives your agent local workflows for generating 3D models
as STEP, GLB, STL or 3MF files. It also does design for manufacturing checks,
generates engineering drawings, and connects to popular 3D printing, sheet metal
and CNC fabrication services.

It is supported by all popular agents that support plugins or the
[skills](https://skills.sh) framework, including Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
Gemini and Grok.

## 💻 Install

### Ask your agent (recommended)

Send this message to your agent and it will install text-to-cad for you.

```text
Install text-to-cad from https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad
```

By default, text-to-cad sends usage stats and crash reports, tagged with a random
ID and never including your files, paths or prompts; turn them off with
`uvx cadgen telemetry off`, or ask your agent to. [Telemetry](#telemetry) says
the rest.

Or install it yourself:

1. CAD runs through [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/): check that it is installed
   (`uv --version`), and if it is missing, install it with
   [uv's installer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/getting-started/installation/).
2. Run the commands under your agent app's heading below, or under
   [Other Agents](#other-agents) if it has none.
3. Restart the app. Its first start downloads CAD's runtime, so it needs a network
   connection.

The plugin for your agent app brings the skills and CAD's viewer, a local server
(`cadgen mcp`). For an agent without a plugin, install the skills alone. Install
one or the other in an app, not both: two copies means every skill twice.

The install commands below take the `latest` branch: it holds the plugin alone
and gets each release once it is on PyPI. `main`, where development happens,
installs too, but can hold changes that aren't released yet. Each app names the
branch in its own way (`#latest`, `--ref latest`, `@latest` or
`--branch latest`); leave it out and the app installs `main`.

Each app's heading also says how to update text-to-cad, and how to reinstall it:
remove it, then install it again. Updating the plugin updates CAD: the new
release's cadgen is downloaded the first time it runs, and the skills and the
server share it. Earlier releases stay in uv's cache until you run `uv cache prune`.

### Claude Code

```bash
claude plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad#latest
claude plugin install text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

The plugin also starts CAD's server. Where Claude Code can show app views, CAD
shows models as viewer cards in the conversation; otherwise, as in a terminal,
asking it to show a model gives you a link that opens the model in the CAD
Viewer in your browser.

To update, run these, then restart Claude Code:

```bash
claude plugin marketplace update earthtojake
claude plugin update text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again:

```bash
claude plugin uninstall text-to-cad@earthtojake
claude plugin marketplace remove earthtojake
```

### Claude Desktop

CAD shows models in the chat: ask Claude to show one and it appears as a viewer
card you can orbit, add to your prompt, and open full size; Claude can read what
you selected and see what you see. It runs locally through uv: add the server to
Claude Desktop's config (Settings > Developer > Edit Config), then restart the
app. If Claude Desktop cannot find `uvx`, give its full path (`which uvx`).

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cad": {
      "command": "uvx",
      "args": ["--no-config", "--managed-python", "--python", "3.13", "--from", "cadgen==0.7.20", "cadgen", "mcp"],
      "env": {"CADGEN_INSTALL_CHANNEL": "claude-desktop"}
    }
  }
}
```

The config pins a cadgen release in `args`, and uvx keeps the version it first
downloads. To update, change that version to the
[latest release](https://pypi.org/project/cadgen/), then restart Claude Desktop.

### Codex

Install text-to-cad from Codex's plugin directory:
[text-to-cad for Codex](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugins_6ac09476ef008191a35887b22b0d048a),
then **Open in desktop app**.

In the Codex app the plugin also brings the CAD viewer: **CAD** in the sidebar
(recent models, and Open), a **CAD** tab beside each thread that the agent
drives, and *Open with CAD* for model files.

<details>
<summary>Manual install</summary>

```bash
codex plugin marketplace add earthtojake/text-to-cad --ref latest
codex plugin add text-to-cad@earthtojake
```

To update, upgrade the `earthtojake` marketplace (or use Plugins › Manage ›
Marketplace), then restart Codex:

```bash
codex plugin marketplace upgrade earthtojake
```

To reinstall, remove it with these, then run the install commands again:

# Repo-source development environment: running tests and tools from a checkout.
#
# The editable cadgen below is what every skill's `cadgen==<VERSION>` requirement
# resolves to locally: sync-version.mjs stamps packages/cadgen/pyproject.toml from
# VERSION, so the editable install reports exactly the pinned version. Installing a
# skill's requirements.txt WITHOUT this file fetches the last published release from
# PyPI instead of the checkout -- this file is the development door.

# pip installs the Python; it cannot build the JavaScript that ships beside it.
# packages/cadgen/src/cadgen/_runtime is gitignored and produced by

# without it, mesh exports, DXF previews, snapshots and the packaged Viewer have
# no runtime to execute, and no build can see what it reads; cadgen names this
# command when it finds none. zig, from this wheel, compiles the native file

=== cadgen pyproject ===
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=77"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "cadgen"
version = "0.7.20"
description = "STEP-first CAD artifact generation runtime: build123d STEP/GLB/topology generation, validation, and inspection for CAD agent skills."
readme = "README.md"
license = "MIT"
license-files = ["LICENSE"]
requires-python = ">=3.11"
authors = [{ name = "earthtojake" }]
keywords = ["cad", "step", "glb", "build123d", "parametric", "agent-skills"]
classifiers = [
  "Development Status :: 4 - Beta",
  "Intended Audience :: Developers",
  "Intended Audience :: Manufacturing",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.11",
  "Programming Language :: Python :: 3.12",
  "Topic :: Multimedia :: Graphics :: 3D Modeling",
  "Topic :: Scientific/Engineering",
]
# ezdxf and shapely both look transitive through build123d, and both are kept
# DIRECT on purpose: cadgen imports each one itself, so each is its own
# dependency regardless of who else happens to pull it in.
#
# ezdxf stopped being a WRITING dependency when @dxf moved to build123d geometry
# (cadgen._internal.dxf_emit) -- the engine writes through build123d's ExportDXF
# and no author-facing contract mentions ezdxf. It remains a READING one, which
# is not going away: cadgen.drawing_payload flattens a .dxf to draw it (for the
# Viewer's pane and for `cadgen dxf snapshot` alike), and cadgen.drawing_checks
# parses one to validate it post-hoc. A DXF reader needs a DXF parser. Dropping the declaration would leave those two modules resting on
# build123d's own dependency list, and they would fail at a user's runtime, not
# at install, the day that list changes.
#
# shapely is likewise narrower than it was -- flatten's unions and offsets are
# OCC operations now, with shapely only the fallback for the degenerate unions
# OCC refuses -- but a fallback that is not installed is not a fallback.
dependencies = [
  # Bounded above on purpose. cadgen does not merely CALL build123d, it
  # reaches into it: the determinism shim shadows `set` in three topology
  # modules and replaces `Vertex.__hash__`, and the lazy store replaces
  # `Compound.__init__` and reads its arguments BY POSITION. A minor release
  # is free to reorder that signature or rename those choke points, and the
  # failure mode is silent: a patch that no longer matches simply stops
  # applying. Raise the ceiling deliberately, after re-running the suite
  # against the new minor.
  "build123d>=0.11.1,<0.12",
  # cadgen imports OCP directly for STEP/XCAF, topology and BREP work.  Match
  # build123d's non-VTK provider: cadgen does not import VTK or cadquery, and
  # this keeps the optional visualization stack out of every CAD install.
  "cadquery-ocp-novtk>=7.9,<8",
  "ezdxf",
  # @eng_drawing renders its PDF through ezdxf's drawing add-on, whose
  # matplotlib backend is the page renderer. The add-on also imports Pillow at
  # module level and ezdxf declares neither, so a cadgen module would otherwise
  # import packages cadgen does not depend on -- and the drawing IS the PDF, so
  # neither is optional.

# DFM review

Provenance: maintained in [earthtojake/text-to-cad](https://github.com/earthtojake/text-to-cad).
Use the installed local skill files as the runtime source of truth.

Produce a process-specific DFM review of the supplied design. This is a guided
review skill, not an automatic feature-recognition or manufacturing
certification engine. Report unavailable checks explicitly.

# CLI for agents

Human-oriented CLIs often block agents: interactive prompts, huge upfront docs, and help text without copy-pasteable examples. Prefer patterns that work headlessly and compose in pipelines.

### Windows 11: Smart App Control

The CAD kernel behind the `cad`, `dxf`, `urdf`, `srdf` and `sdf`
skills is `OCP`, OpenCascade's Python binding, and its wheel ships an unsigned
native module. Windows 11's Smart App Control blocks unsigned native code, so
on a machine where it is on (the default on a fresh install) every `cadgen`
command and `import build123d` fails with
`ImportError: DLL load failed while importing OCP`, and Event Viewer records
the refusal as Event ID 3077 under CodeIntegrity › Operational. `cadgen doctor`
names this when it sees it.

Smart App Control has no per-app exception. Either turn it off (Settings ›
Privacy & security › Windows Security › App & browser control › Smart App
Control settings; once off it can only be turned back on by reinstalling
Windows) or run the CAD skills under WSL, where it does not apply. The wheel
is built by the cadquery-ocp project, so signing it is not something this
repository can do.

## 🧰 Skills

Install the library to give agents focused workflows for CAD, fabrication,
robot description files, simulation, and local review.

| Skill        | Summary                                                                                                                                            | Source                                              |
| ------------ | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- |
| CAD          | Creates and edits CAD models from plain-language or image requests, with STEP as the main output along with options to export to STL, 3MF and GLB. | [skills/cad](skills/cad/SKILL.md)                   |
| step.parts   | Finds off-the-shelf STEP parts like screws, bearings, motors, and connectors.                                                                      | [skills/step-parts](skills/step-parts/SKILL.md)     |
| Engineering Drawing | Dimensioned engineering drawings from a part, as a PDF: views, hidden lines, dimensions, hole callouts, title block. | [skills/engineering-drawing](skills/engineering-drawing/SKILL.md) |
| DXF          | Creates 2D DXF drawings like profiles, templates, gaskets, and cut layouts from Python sources or CAD geometry.                                    | [skills/dxf](skills/dxf/SKILL.md)                   |
| URDF         | Writes robot structure files with links, joints, limits, inertials, and meshes.                                                                    | [skills/urdf](skills/urdf/SKILL.md)                 |
| SRDF         | Adds MoveIt planning groups, end effectors, poses, and collision rules to a URDF.                                                                  | [skills/srdf](skills/srdf/SKILL.md)                 |
| SDF          | Creates simulator models and worlds with frames, physics, sensors, and lights.                                                                     | [skills/sdf](skills/sdf/SKILL.md)                   |
| SendCutSend  | Checks DXF and STEP files before upload to SendCutSend.                                                                                            | [skills/sendcutsend](skills/sendcutsend/SKILL.md)   |
| DfAM Check   | Measures mesh printability per process: wall thickness, overhangs, support volume, and build orientation.                                          | [skills/dfam-check](skills/dfam-check/SKILL.md)     |
| DFM | Reviews a part for sheet metal, CNC machining, or injection molding, with measured evidence and the cited rule behind every finding; measures draft, undercuts and projected area from a mesh. | [skills/dfm](skills/dfm/SKILL.md) |
| G-code       | Slices models into printer-ready G-code with OrcaSlicer, using your own printer presets.                                                           | [skills/gcode](skills/gcode/SKILL.md)               |
| Bambu Labs   | Sends prints to Bambu Lab printers through Bambu Connect, Bambu Lab's official app, or Bambu Studio.                                               | [skills/bambu-labs](skills/bambu-labs/SKILL.md)     |

The store contains only derived results\n\n`~/.cache/cadgen` is the store: content-addressed objects (a model's result\ntree and the components it is made of) and input-addressed index entries\n(the per-model record, the document → tree map, bounds and tessellation\nentries) — data derivable from sources and documents, and nothing else. Its\nlayout, formats, gate, two-sides law and invariants are the contract in\n[`STORE.md`](STORE.md); read it before touching anything that writes to or\nreads from the store. Where this document and `STORE.md` disagree, `STORE.md`\nis right and this one is stale.\n\n*Pressure-test*: everything in the store is (a) a pure function of some\nsource or document, (b) safely deletable at any time, and (c) rebuildable\nby running the models again. If losing a store entry would lose information,\nthat information is in the wrong place.\n\n**The store is what the sources imply; the sidecar is what the author meant.**\n\nThe store holds itself to a size cap (`CADGEN_STORE_MAX`, default 20 GB): the\ndaemon, when idle, evicts derived entries (mesh, surface, component, bounds,\ndrawing) least recently written first and sweeps what nothing reaches, and\nretires on sight the index kinds an older cadgen left (`index/op`). A record,\na document entry or an output entry is never evicted. `cadgen store gc` does\nthe same by hand (`STORE.md` §8). A cadgen never judges what it cannot read:\na store a newer cadgen wrote to within 30 days is left to that cadgen, and a\nfolder it does not know is never touched. A read never writes the store, and a write\nthat finds its bytes already present claims them, so deletion needs no\ncoordination: a sweep keeps whatever a publish has claimed, and a racing\nreader re-misses and rebuilds. Store correctness needs\nno lock protocol: atomic writes, pins and the publish rule (`STORE.md` §5, §7)\ndecide concurrent outcomes. Saved-file readers never wait for a source model\nto finish; missing derived artifacts are resolved through the build pool.\n*Pressure-test*: build a model and snapshot it, make the store read-only, then\ndo both again: each succeeds and nothing under the store changes.\n\n### 3. One sidecar per artifact, and it belongs to that artifact alone\n\n`part.step` gets `part.step.json` — schema-versioned sections (kinematics,\nappearance, animation). New capability = new section + schema bump, never a second sidecar\nfile. Model-side, beside the artifact, so it travels with the file it\ndescribes — and it exists only when law 17 says it must.\n\nA sidecar describes the model that declared it — never its parent, never its\nchildren. A parent composing a child receives geometry and intrinsic appearance\n(tree, labels, colors, PBR values, placements, exact shape). The child's\nkinematics belong to the child's own sidecar,\nand an assembly that needs a relation declares it on the assembly. This is\nwhat lets a cached child stand in for its function: the cache carries\ngeometry and intrinsic appearance; a parent never reads the child's sidecar.\n*Pressure-test*: build a child that declares `kinematics=`, then build a parent\nthat composes it. The parent's kinematics section contains only its own\ndeclarations, and the child's sidecar is unchanged by the parent's build.\nIntrinsic finishes travel with the pinned geometry and are rebound to the\nparent document's occurrences when it is saved.\n\n### 4. Zero metadata in written artifacts\n\nA STEP or DXF is pure geometry. Provenance, kinematics, and context ride\nthe sidecar; the artifact separated from everything else is a plain\nimportable file.\n\n### 5. Byte determinism is the writers' promise, not the kernel's\n\ncadgen's writers are pure: the same shapes give the same bytes, in every\nformat — STEP (canonicalized NAUO ids and presentation-style ordering), meshes\n(one deterministic tessellator), DXF (geometry-ordered emitter). The geometry\nkernel makes no such promise. Two runs of one model can differ in a last digit\nor in the order of the pieces a boolean returns, and cadgen neither hides that\nnor depends on it. Equal bytes mean reuse; different bytes cost a\nrecomputation (a re-mesh, a parent recompose) and never a wrong answer. A\nrebuild whose writer input is unchanged keeps its saved STEP instead of writing\nthe same bytes again ([`STORE.md`](STORE.md) §3, `writerInput`).\nContent addresses stay byte hashes; whether a model runs is decided by its\nsources (`STORE.md` §4), never by its outputs being reproducible. Compare two\nbuilds by geometry within a tolerance, never by file hash.\n*Pressure-test*: build one model twice, each from an empty store. If the bytes\ndiffer, nothing fails, and the second build's outputs are as correct as the\nfirst's.\n\n### 6. One surface, three faces\n\nThe DECORATOR declares a capability on a model, the PUBLIC FUNCTION\n(`cadgen.<format>.<verb>`) performs it, and the CLI (`cadgen <format>\n<verb>`) is GENERATED from the function's signature\n(`_internal/cli_from_function.py`) — never hand-written, structurally\nsync-tested.\n\n*Pressure-test*: for any option, \
build123d geometry; `read_scene(path)` returns\nrevision-scoped occurrence/selector views with caller-owned world geometry.\n`cadgen.geometry` provides `closest_points`, `overlap_volume`, `is_sound`,\n`topology_errors`, `boundary_edges`, `self_intersections` and\n`mass_properties`. These operations accept native geometry and return facts;\nselection, units, thresholds, exclusions and verdicts belong to the caller's\nscript. The inspect\nCLI and `step.inspect` are removed, with an immediate migration error.\nThe contracts live in [`step_scene.py`](src/cadgen/step_scene.py) and\n[`geometry.py`](src/cadgen/geometry.py). They import no kernel at namespace\nload and require no display artifacts.\n\n**The one exception: `@eng_drawing` has no public function and no CLI.**\n`cadgen.eng_drawing` declares a capability on a DOCUMENT OVER a part, not on a\nmodel: what it consumes is a `Sheet` the author composed in Python — views,\ntheir placement, and dimensions between points on the part's geometry — and no\nargument list can carry that. There is nothing for a generated CLI to take but\na script path, which law 7 forbids, and nothing for a public function to add\nover the decorator. The decorator is the whole surface; the script is the\nprogram; the output is one PDF. Adding a `cadgen eng-drawing` verb would mean\npassing a script to a CLI, so it stays absent by design.\n\n### 7. Documents-only CLIs; scripts are programs\n\n`python model.py` is the one source door: it gates, builds, writes every\noutput the decorators declare (`.step`, meshes, sidecar — STEP is one output\nkind, not a required one), and rewrites declared exports that drifted. Every\nCLI takes documents, resolves them by their bytes, and compiles a missing\ntree from those bytes as a job in the build pool — never from a script.\n\nA script is a program, and cadgen runs it wherever it lives. The import path\ninside a build is exactly `python script.py`'s — the script's own folder, then\nthe caller's `PYTHONPATH` — and nothing cadgen adds or infers from directory\nnames. Project layout (`src/`, `lib/`, format folders) is a convention of the\nskills, never a fact cadgen knows; a project that wants an import root beyond\nthe script's folder declares it the standard Python way (`PYTHONPATH=src`).\n*Pressure-test*: move a project's folders around and rebuild; cadgen must not\ncare, only the project's imports may.\n\nA script may declare several models, and builds the ones its `__main__` calls.\nIts flags (`--force`, `--json`, `--verbose`, the mesh tolerances) apply to every\nmodel it builds: no flag names, selects or configures one of them. A command\nthat addresses one model, such as `cadgen store why`, names it\n`script.py::function`; a bare `script.py` names its sole model, and a file that\ndeclares several must be named. *Pressure-test*: put two models in one file and\ncall both from `__main__`; every flag must mean the same thing for each.\n\n### 8. No backwards compatibility\n\nHard cutovers only. Every retired surface fails loudly with a teaching\nerror naming its replacement — never an alias, never a shim.\n\nThe explicit exception is `cadgen.assembly.AssemblyHelper`: it is softly\ndeprecated and still works. Construction emits a visible `FutureWarning`\npointing to native build123d compounds, labels, transforms and joints.\nImporting it is quiet; a current model that skips its body emits no warning.\nThis does not change geometry, model freshness or child sharing.\n\n### 9. Closed vocabularies\n\nEvery declaration surface has a closed key/kind set. Unknown keys are\nteaching errors, never silently ignored.\n\n### 10. Loud failure or correct output, nothing between\n\nThe cardinal sin is plausible-wrong output at exit 0. No silent fallbacks,\nno globs, no guessing; a failed render leaves NO file at the requested\npath.\n\n### 11–14. Runtime laws (shared with the bundled JavaScript runtime)\n\nKinematics is pure data and choreography is pure JS, fully independent\n(11). Clients render from file + sidecar + the store's artifact side and never\nread source, a record, or trigger source builds (12). A build's status\n(STORE §9b) carries no geometry: clients render the saved file.\nCorrectness never depends on a\nstore hit (13). Composition: importing binds, calling links — a parent\ndepends on a child by its RESULT (the pinned tree) and on what importing it\nruns in the parent's process (its module body and model headers, never a\nmodel body), on a constant by its VALUE, on a helper by its REACH (the part of\nthe helper the script and every file the build executed can run, closed\nstatically; the whole file — or the whole closure — wherever the analysis\ncannot see), on a data file by its BYTES (every file the build opened,\nwhoever opened it: STORE.md §5, every read is seen),\nand on every file whose appearance would change what an import finds\n([`STORE.md`](STORE.md) §3) — and a model must never `read_step` its own\noutput (14). The bundled runtime\nunder `_runtime/` is the JS half of these; the laws' JS statements live in that\nruntime. It is built\nwhen the wheel is packaged and travels only inside it: the source tree never\ncarries a built copy, so an installed cadgen and the sources that produced it\ncannot disagree.\n\n### 15. The package ships alone\n\nThe installed distribution is the whole world: the Python engine, the\nbundled `_runtime/`, and this document. It works with the repository it\nwas built from gone — and its markdown must read that way, referring to\nnothing outside the package.\n\n*Pressure-test*: every sentence in the package's markdown must be true and\nactionable for someone who only ran `pip install cadgen`. build123d's `==` and `is_same` answer. A script therefore behaves the\nsame inside cadgen as under plain Python. The hooks that remain change no\nresult: `determinism.py` fixes the iteration order of build123d's\nde-duplications (an order-keeping set, and a `Vertex` hash by point that\nleaves equality alone), lazy children defer a child's geometry until it is\nread (`STORE.md` §9a), and the file trace only watches what the run opens\n(`STORE.md` §5). An expensive or independently edited part gets its\nspeed by being its own model, never from a cache inside one. What an older\ncadgen cached inside a run (`index/op`, the operation cache) is never read,\nand is retired with every object only it named (`STORE.md` §8).\n*Pressure-test*: call a model's function under plain Python and inside a\ncadgen build; the geometry it returns, and the answer to every `==` and\n`is_same` along the way, are the same.\n\n### 19. Nothing waits on the network\n\nOnce installed, cadgen works offline: every command, build, snapshot, server\nand page. Its own requests are two: telemetry\n(`analytics.py`, usage counts under a random id, sent by default once a `cadgen`\ncommand has said so, and never after the person's no) and the daily version check\n(`updates.py`). Both run in the background and fail silently: no start,\ncommand, build, request or tool call waits on them, and one that fails changes\nnothing but what is counted or offered. A command sends nothing itself: it hands\nwhat it counted -- a build it made with no daemon to ask, a snapshot, a drawing, a\ncrash -- to a running build daemon over its local socket, never starting one, and\ngives up after a moment (`daemon.client.HAND_OVER_SECONDS`); with no daemon to take\nit, it keeps it in a small file beside the settings for the next process that sends\n(`analytics.spool`). A process that exits sends nothing either: its last batch --\na server's, or the build daemon's -- is kept in a file beside the settings, and the\nnext process that sends sends it in the background, a moment after it starts\n(`analytics.KEPT`). One wait remains, bounded, for something only the network can\ndo: `cadgen telemetry off`, which waits for the deletion it asks for (still owed,\nand asked again, when nobody answers). The\npages load nothing from the internet: everything they show ships in the wheel.\nInstalling needs the network (cadgen itself, and the headless browser the first\nsnapshot fetches), and nothing after it does. The law is the package's, not the\nlauncher's: a launcher that checks a package index before it starts anything\n(`uvx`, once its cache is stale) has its own needs.\n*Pressure-test*: with an installed cadgen and every request refused (a proxy on\na closed port), and again with every request hanging, start a server, open a\nview, call each tool, and run a build and a snapshot: each works, and nothing\nwaits on a request beyond the two waits above.\n\n## The shape of the package\n\n```\nsrc/cadgen/\n  <format>.py            # ### **Assistant**

收到——**配套工具是硬要求**（工具不在表里，Codex 根本调不到，等于白做）。这条我记进本轮的验收项：**每个能力都必须有模型可调的工具 + 常驻指令点名**。

后台调研也回来了，两个关键事实很值：
- **cursor/plugins**：技能**就是标准 `SKILL.md`**（100 条清单在 `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json`）⇒ **技能正文可移植**，但 hooks/agents/宿主目录不可。
- **text-to-cad**：能出 **GLB** ⇒ 正好能用我们**现有的 3D 预览窗**看；依赖里 OCP 轮子 **87MB**、且首次运行要联网下载 CAD runtime。

先清掉我卡住的校验进程，然后开工 P1。

进程清掉了，集成点也摸清了。开始 P1 落地 —— 先写**引擎模块**（把我验证过的脚本搬成正式模块，含路径可信根闸）。

引擎模块写好了。现在写 IPC 域 + 接进 manifest/registry/composition（先看清 composition 的条目格式）。

域写好了。用脚本把三处注册（manifest / registry / composition）**按格式插入**，避免手改出错。

`manifest` 与 `ipc-registry` 已插 ✓（composition 那条是**最后一个条目**，块尾正则没匹配）。看尾部再定点插。

插入写出了**尾逗号**（非法 JSON）。看当前尾部并修。

composition 修好（**87 个域**，含 html-video ✓）。跑生成器（IPC 桥 + 域组合层）。

生成器跑通（449 方法 / 87 域 ✓）。它提示 `html-video` 缺**能力描述**（这份描述就是模型读的技能清单）—— 补上，再做**模型可调的工具**。

形状清楚了（顺带发现**一个我自己的尾巴**：`wallpaper_set` 的可选模式还写着已退役的 `vanta` ⇒ 得改成 `stars`）。一并把工具、描述、以及那条尾巴都补上。

四处都接上了（含修掉我那条 `vanta` 尾巴）。重跑生成器 + 类型检查。

类型全绿（electron + 渲染层都是 0 错），能力技能里也有了 html-video。**现在做真链路验证**：直接调应用里的这个通道，出一段 MP4。

真链路验证跑着（应用里直接调这条通道出 MP4 + 试非法源被拒），等结果。

#### Thinking

The user reminds: "配套工具记得完善好哦，没有工具codex调用不了的" — remember to complete the supporting TOOLS: without a tool, Codex can't call it.

That's an important product rule (already in AGENTS.md: "工具在表里模型不主动用 = 白配"; and dynamicTools/gateway registration is required for the model to call anything).

So for P1 (HTML→MP4) I MUST register a **dynamicTool / gateway capability** so Codex can actually call it — otherwise it's dead code.

Let me acknowledge and factor that in: each of P1–P4 that produces a capability must have:
- a dynamicTool (or a `harness_tools` gateway entry),
- plus the 常驻指令 (developer-instructions) mention so the model knows to use it,
- plus a built-in skill (for how-to).

And the research agent returned great facts:

**cursor/plugins**:
- `.cursor-plugin/marketplace.json` — 100 entries; fields name/source/description.
- Skills ARE standard SKILL.md ✓ (with possible extra keys icon/color/license — our engine tolerates extra frontmatter keys? Hmm — need to check; the engine may ignore unknown keys ✓ likely).
- No install mechanism in the repo; host-driven. Many plugins contain Cursor-specific parts (agents/, hooks/, rules/*.mdc, .cursor-plugin/plugin.json, mcp.json) → **skill bodies portable, hooks/agents/host dirs not**.
- License: no root LICENSE; per-plugin MIT.
- Categories: Developer Tools / Utilities / Productivity / Integrations; 17 root plugins + ~95 third_party.

So P2's compatibility conclusion: **技能正文可移植**（标准 SKILL.md）→ a third source is viable **for the `skills/` subsets**, not for the whole plugin package.

**text-to-cad**:
- 3 entry points: MCP (`uvx ... cadgen mcp`), 12 skills, CLI `cadgen <format> <verb>`.
- Deps: build123d, cadquery-ocp-novtk (OCP, 87MB wheel), ezdxf, shapely, playwright, matplotlib/Pillow; dfam-check needs trimesh/numpy/rtree/scipy/networkx/lxml. First-run downloads a CAD runtime (network needed).
- License: repo MIT; OCP/build123d on PyPI marked Apache-2.0; OCCT itself needs separate verification.
- Outputs: STEP/STL/3MF/GLB ✓ (GLB = our 3D viewer can preview it directly!! ✓✓)
- Manufacturing checks: dfm/dfam-check.

import { teamRunStore } from "../runtime-refs";
import { defineFeature } from "../context";
import type { IpcHost } from "../ipc-host";

export const teamRunsFeature = defineFeature<null>({
  id: "team-runs",
  inject: ["ipc"],
  setup: (ctx) => {
    const ipcHost = ctx.get<IpcHost>("ipc");
    if (!ipcHost) throw new Error("team-runs: 缺少 ipc 服务（宿主未提供）");

    ipcHost.handle("team-runs:list", async (_event, threadId: string) => teamRunStore.listRuns(String(threadId ?? "")));

    ctx.effect(() => {
      ipcHost.removeHandler("team-runs:list");
    });
  },
});

/**
 * html-video-ipc（P1，2026-10-11）
 * 域：html-video(1)
 * 通道：html-video:render（本地 HTML/URL → MP4）
 */
import { app } from "electron";
import path from "node:path";
import { defineFeature } from "../context";
import type { IpcHost } from "../ipc-host";
import { renderHtmlToVideo } from "../html-video";

export const htmlVideoFeature = defineFeature<null>({
  id: "html-video",
  inject: ["ipc"],
  setup: (ctx) => {
    const ipcHost = ctx.get<IpcHost>("ipc");
    if (!ipcHost) throw new Error("html-video: 缺少 ipc 服务（宿主未提供）");
    ipcHost.handle("html-video:render", async (_e, input: { source?: string; seconds?: number; fps?: number; width?: number; height?: number; outPath?: string }) => {
      const out = input?.outPath && input.outPath.trim()

/**
 * team-runs-ipc（10-03 从 `features/teams-agents-ipc.ts` 按前缀拆出，同时改为**插件形态**）
 *
 * 域：team-runs(1)
 * 通道：team-runs:list（某会话的运行记录）
 *
 * 运行记录的**写入方**在 `teams-ipc` 的 `beginRun`/`finishRun`（调度路径），本域只做查询面。
 */
import { teamRunStore } from "../runtime-refs";
import { defineFeature } from "../context";
import type { IpcHost } from "../ipc-host";

export const teamRunsFeature = defineFeature<null>({
  id: "team-runs",
  inject: ["ipc"],
  setup: (ctx) => {
    const ipcHost = ctx.get<IpcHost>("ipc");
    if (!ipcHost) throw new Error("team-runs: 缺少 ipc 服务（宿主未提供）");

    ipcHost.handle("team-runs:list", async (_event, threadId: string) => teamRunStore.listRuns(String(threadId ?? "")));

    ctx.effect(() => {
      ipcHost.removeHandler("team-runs:list");
    });
  },
});
